The biggest issue was the door knob had snapped off. I had some non-toxic epoxy that I used to fix it. Just glad I put together ahead of time. By Christmas it would be solid and sturdy.

No matter how I adjusted the pieces that held the "wall" together it would not stay within the groove designed to hold it in place, and one of the floors was peeling out of the box. A little tape fixed this and I doubt it will be noticed, but irritated me a bit. I'm grateful it wasn't worse and I could make it work/fix but it shouldn't have been needed. If I hadn't set it up early we may have had a few tears (and daddy words) when opened.

Now, overall I think it's going to be a hit and I'm sure she'll play with it for hours. I'm giving it 2 stars based on quality though. You may not have the same issues, but I'd be prepared just in case.

Melissa & Doug Flower Jewelry Box Yes, I received this item for free... but I have also purchased this product for full price retail, so trust me when I say this is a great toy!

In a world full of plastic toys, wooden toys really shine in my personal opinion. Over the years, we have owned a variety of Melissa and Doug toys, and although some have been better than others, we have come to expect quality from this brand... This DIY jewelry box does NOT disappoint! My girls (ages 6--8) really enjoyed decorating these. Not only that, but the first jewelry box we owned lasted over 2 years and through multiple bath times (you heard right, it was actually converted into a pink swimming pool lol). But even through all that creative abuse, it never broke and the only reason I threw it away was because I was scared the fabric inside would start to mold. But never once did any of the hinges come loose, nor were there any other functional problems during the entire lifespan of this toy. Also, as a side benefit, I have found that kid-friendly storage devices like these really encourage organizational skills :)

In summary, if I could give this product more stars, I would. A winner from M&D!!!

text_fidelity_a:
Anki DRIVE Starter Kit (Previous Version) This idea is absolutely amazing. My kids were in awe of it as we opened the box and set up the track. The first times around the track there were some issues with figuring out the controls but all in all it was an amazing experience. The cars eerily control themselves around the huge 4 foot by 8 foot track. The were mesmerized while controlling the cars in and out of lanes. They really do work like slot cars, but with a wide open track.

However, after racing for a little while, my kids started getting frustrated that the cars would occasionally go into a spin and shoot off the track or end up heading the wrong direction, which they would quickly notice and reverse, but it was frustrating when your car would spin and start going the wrong way. Often you would see a car fly off the track and be told to return the car to the track. It happens enough to be intrusive to the game.

The battling aspect of the game is great. The cars do seem to have a sense of aim when firing. But we did run into a little trouble. My older son ended up playing with his car for an hour, building up points and adding upgrades to his car. Now his car is heads and shoulders above my youngest's and there is frustration for my youngest since they are no longer competing on par.

We are still in awe of the technology and we still enjoy playing with it, but it is a little short of perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Anki DRIVE Starter Kit (Previous Version)

text_fidelity_a:
2058 Pieces City Police Mobile Command Truck Toy Building Blocks Set for Kids, Boys Age 6+, with Police Station, Police Cars, Airplane, Helicopter, Boat, 2022 Newest Police Toy Gift for Police Fans This is one of the better kits that this brand makes. They're compatible with LEGO, albeit of a lower quality overall, and this is another of their designs that don't come with minifigs, and which isn't inherently designed for them. You'll make model police vehicles, but your LEGO dudes won't go riding around in them - they simply won't fit.

The other big downside is that you don't get to do the bags in order like you do with LEGO. You kind of have to open them all at once and work from one gigantic pile in the center of the table. It's messy and can lead to quitting, but that's all part of the experience.

They will fit somewhat within the tractor component, which is the largest piece of this set, and by far the most interesting. There are a number of playable aspects to this that give you a lot more bang for your buck than the more model-focused kits we've tried from Wishalife previously.

Overall, there's plenty of bricks, OK instructions, a large number of stickers, and plenty of fun to be had here. No, it's not LEGO, but it's not too bad considering. This is a great buy to keep your kids playing for some time.
text_fidelity_b: 2058 Pieces City Police Mobile Command Truck Toy Building Blocks Set for Kids, Boys Age 6+, with Police Station, Police Cars, Airplane, Helicopter, Boat, 2022 Newest Police Toy Gift for Police Fans

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Games UNO NFL LVII Card Game for Kids, Adults, Family and Game Night with Special "Touchdown" Rule for 2-10 Players Ok hear me out for a minute before I explain why I didn't give it a better rating. My wife and I love The Office. We consider ourselves huge fans-- buuut maybe not quite to the point of super fans because we can be forgetful on certain things about the show occasionally. But we are those people that, if you tell us a story, we'll likely have an Office reference to match it. So we were excited about getting to try this out.

This is where I might be a little too picky about it…well, I'm just going to say a little passionate about it lol. But if it's a classic game with a different theme (such as this one)-- it's usually directed toward people who are big fans of that specific theme...that likely will be expecting certain details. Otherwise, if they aren't fans, or real into that theme, they will probably just get the classic/original version...or go for a different theme that they are fans of. So if you're leaving big parts out, you're likely going to have some disappointed fans.

I also realize that there's so much great things about the show and so I'm sure it's hard to narrow it all down to a select amount of cards. So I give some credit to that.

My reasons for rating it lower:

Nearly all of the cards are of Michael, Dwight, Jim and Pam. Then there's randomly one of Kelly and the special rule/twist card with Kevin....but no one else is part of the game?! And yes, the ones included are amazing actors/characters and all...but many of the other regulars are, too- and all together they made The Office.

There are cards for numbers 0-9 (they each have the different colors) and 6 action cards. So that's 16 different pictures they could utilize. Which means there are enough to feature the regular characters…I'll list/count out the ones that come to my mind 1-Michael, 2-Dwight, 3-Jim, 4-Pam, 5-Angela, 6.Kevin, 7-Oscar, 8-Creed, 9-Meredith, 10-Stanley, 11-Phyllis, 12-Kelly, 13-Ryan, 14-Toby, 15-Darryl.

I also felt like some of the photos could have been better selected. I won't rant on too much about that, and spare you, but a quick example-- Kevin's chili twist card isn't of that actual scene just him at his desk. And why not put Toby as the draw 4 card, instead 😄

I do like the picture of the back-side of the cards, the wild card with Michael dancing in the Diwali episode and *some* of the other pics they chose.

The card and photo quality is really good. My box container was torn a little at the top.

It is still fun to play, I do like the special rule/twist for Kevin's chili, and like the idea of The Office theme but I do think it could be improved upon by including more characters.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games UNO NFL LVII Card Game for Kids, Adults, Family and Game Night with Special "Touchdown" Rule for 2-10 Players

text_fidelity_a: CGE Czech Games Edition Codenames Boardgame This game is best played with 4 people (two teams of two).  Your partner tries to prompt you to pick the correct cards on the table between you by giving you a single word clue and telling you how many cards on the table it relates to.  You need to decipher the hint by figuring out which of the cards they means, but don't pick the wrong one!  It could end up giving a point to the other team or if you pick the one "black card" on the table it ends the game and you instantly lose.  This game is endlessly creative and challenging as the word cards on the table and which cards correspond to your team will always be different each game.  The creative part is figuring out new ways to bundle the most cards together with a single word so you can find all your teams cards before the other team finds theirs.  It's a race to figure out the code!

Educational Insights Pass The Peas This game has potential, but due to its flimsy nature and low quality of organization, we didn't enjoy it as much as we could have.

The peas are just press out cardboard pieces that sit on top of cardboard pods. They are slippery and as you pass the pods, the peas slide everywhere. If you are at any size table with people sitting average distance apart, the peas will easily slip off and get messed up as you pass them.

The little bags of peas also should be color coded. Instead all of the bags are supposed to match an individual pea pod, but you have to open them up every time to look as on the outside they are all identical. At very least, they should have put in different colored strings so you could see which was what.

If they made the pods so they would lay flat instead of bending closed somewhat, and maybe have something like Velcro or magnetic surface, it would be a lot better to use. As you move around the pods it would be more secure and not so stressful.

The game has potential to be fun, but a combination of the cheap way it is made and the frustration present when trying to play, it just isn't as nice as it should be. The game is somewhat fun at first, but soon after beginning to play we just lost interest.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Pass The Peas

Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed(for the most part).

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost, and it provides great "rest" points. It kind of made me wonder what the point of all the bags were in this set.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers just ache after working with Mega Blocks due to the amount of pressure required to get some of the pieces together. Some of the pieces were incredibly frustrating to get together. Not only that but some of the parts from the final product keep falling off/apart. It took so long to put the thing together(with so much pain) that it almost brings some tears to see parts fall off. ;)

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

In defense of Mega Bloks, though, the little figurines are way cooler, and they have soft parts! IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cool! (I just found it a pain. Literally.)
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks TMNT Collectors Krang's Rampage Building Kit

Hot Wheels Track Builder Spiral Stack-Up Track Set This HOT WHEELS TRACK BUILDER SPIRAL STACK-UP set is a terrific choice for expanding an existing Hot Wheels track layout, as long as you have a fair amount of floor or table space. It's a really large stunt that's about five feet long when it's assembled according to the boxed instructions (though the launcher ramps can be rearranged, using two towers instead of one, to use less space).

The way this set works, is that the first car launched from the top of the tower launches two more cars (not included with the set) as it speeds down the ramp, then triggers a release that dumps a car off the second level of the "box" located at the end of the double ramp, until it finally exits the stunt through the lower level of the "box". The second car that is launched (by the first car) speeds down a long ramp that is connected near the top of the tower, and exits the stunt. The third car that is launched travels down a short ramp and stops on the second level of the exit "box", waiting to for the first car to dump it.

There's a lot of action that makes me smile in this track builder set. Also, the two cars that actually exit the setup have a lot of momentum left that will carry them elsewhere in a well-designed layout. One of the best things about this setup is that all three cars usually complete the entire run flawlessly, without jumping the track or losing momentum or stopping too soon. The "Nitrium" car that comes with the set is a fairly heavy one, because the set works best with a weighty car starting in the top position.

For me, this Hot Wheels playset was a little more challenging to assemble than others that I've set up. As always, the key thing is to identify your parts correctly, and to keep looking until you find the right place to make a connection if you don't understand the instructions right away. The color-coding of the plastic parts helped me with one confusing part--the set has two red launcher arms that attach to a yellow base, and one gray launcher lever that attaches to a gray base. In my customer photos, there are three cars loaded into the set--the orange/white car at the very top is the included Nitrium car.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Track Builder Spiral Stack-Up Track Set

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice These dice are beautifully made of solid pine. Playing games with these are fun but play responsibly. Displaying the dice as works of art is equally as great.

Provided in the package:
- Six die that weigh a combined 4.6 pounds. (See the attached pictures for an idea of size relative to two of my cats and their water fountain.)
- A strong canvas pouch for carrying the dice.
- A folded one-page pamphlet with two game variations and a sample score card for copying.

Each die is beautiful and each "number point" (i.e. dots) on the same die face is painted a rich coffee brown or dark tan. However, the "number points" are various shades of coffee brown on each side of the same die, so there is a slight inconsistency in color there. Nevertheless, this does not take away from their beauty. One should discount the "life-sized" claim. They are large but all of them stacked three high, side-by-side, do not even reach the height of a poised cat as you can see from my photos. When used for play instead of art, the round edge of each die provides for a smooth roll and reduction of injury to property or person. Although this is rated for ages 6 and above, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND children, adults, and pets stay far back when rolling the dice.

My boyfriend and I played the first game on my inside carpet since it was raining outside. I made sure to remove any items that could break around the area we were playing and I had to keep shooing the cats away. I originally thought we had to roll all six die at once (which is impossible). Therefore, when playing the two games in the instructions, roll each die one at a time because they are too large to roll together. The instructions should say that, however, because the first thought I had is "How am I going to roll these six die all at once," when the instructions said "roll the dice"?

My boyfriend loved the dice and the game even though I won. Since each die is heavy, it is extremely important to throw each die gently. I can see unsupervised children or drunk adults throwing these at each other and causing serious damage or death. As long as everyone plays responsibly, hours of fun and friendly competition are awaiting those who play this lawn or carpeted basement "game."
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Giant Wooden Dice

text_fidelity_a:
Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game Onitama is a 2-player only game that tries to have a theme, but is really quite abstract.

When I heard about it, I was really quite intrigued that this would be added to the Dice Tower Essentials line as an abstract; after all, isn't Tom Vasel the guy who dislikes most abstracts because they're not theme-y enough? Yet here is the third game in his very quality game series that is otherwise highly thematic, and he goes with an abstract. Seemed like the game must be incredible to have cracked that list as an abstract.

I played a number of times with my wife, who admittedly likes this game quite a lot more than I do. I find the game similar to chess or the Duke, in which you have a certain number of moves, represented by cards, and you move your pieces around the board, switching cards with your opponent along the way. There is a lot of doublethink - If I do this, then they know I'll do that next turn, so they might do this... - and I like that element of the game, but the limitation on my moves did tend to cramp my style a little more, and I'd find myself wishing I just had more options. That skill can probably be built up over time playing with this one, but I don't know if it grabbed me enough to make me invest my time with it.

If 3.5 were an option, I'd go with that. Just not my style, and not as good as the expectations led me to believe.
text_fidelity_b: Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions [[VIDEOID:moOM6Q7TMDWRNW]]This is like an awesome mix between Apples to Apples and Trivial Pursuit. It's played very similarly to Apples to Apples, but you have an open-ended question, and everyone writes answers down on a piece of paper. Then the pieces of paper are handed in, and the person who is It has to guess who wrote what question. The person who is It gets one point per right answer that they match with the people playing the game.

It's a fun, and simple concept, which makes for a fun and simple game. And, the questions are awesome. I've gotten a few "getting to know you" books in the past, which have lists of supposedly interesting questions. All of those books pale in comparison to this awesome game. These questions are intense, interesting, and none of them put too much pressure on you.

My girlfriend and I found ourselves just reading the questions and answering them a lot, just by ourselves. It's a great way to talk about tons of different topics than the ones that usually come up. Like I said, these questions are great.

I usually really don't like party games like this. I usually like strategy games better. But this is one party game that I love.

Pros:
+Awesome questions
+Fun game
+Good quality
+Well designed

Cons:
-You need 4 people to play according to the rules, even though these are fun questions to ask if there are just two or three of you
text_fidelity_b: All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions

text_fidelity_a:
The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends…… If you're familiar with the game Spyfall, then you're going to be able to jump right into this game. This one is quirkier, faster, but fortunately, has more replayability than Spyfall does.

In The Chameleon, each player is given a code card, or a card that says "You're the Chameleon." If you have a code card, you look up a word on a shared board, and if you're The Chameleon, you attempt to blend in with everyone else. After a little bit of finding and thinking time, each player says one word, even the Chameleon. Each player is then to attempt to argue and deduce who the Chameleon player is. Everyone votes, and that player is revealed. If it's not the Chameleon, then that player has done a good job of blending in and is the winner of the round. If it is the Chameleon, then that player gets the opportunity to guess the secret word that everyone else knew. If they get it right, they win. If not, everyone else wins.

Rounds of this game are fast, and that's a great thing. After repeat plays, it becomes fairly easy to identify the Chameleon player, but that's when the game really starts. Were you vague enough with your words so that they cannot figure out the secret code word?

There is enough replayability in this box to make the game fun for a wide range of groups, and a larger number of players. There are 40 different category clues, which means that there are 640 different possible words you could have, and that far exceeds the 20 locations of Spyfall.

Two issues prevent this from being a 5* game. The first is component quality. It's bad. Cards are awkwardly sized and flimsy, there are remainder marks on the edges of some cards from where they were cut. The second issue is that there simply aren't enough mapping location cards in the box. There's really only two possible sets of locations, and while there are no players who will be able to memorize the exact locations of words, it's possible that repeat mappings occur, and Chameleons with outstanding memories will be able to guess with regularity by reading the dice.
text_fidelity_b: The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends……

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

This model is made of wood. It shows to have 47 pieces. There are 3 boards with the cutout pieces. You’ll want to use caution when removing the pieces from the boards so that you do not break them. You remove the pieces from the boards as you go. The pieces are numbered on the instruction sheet, but not on the boards. So if you remove them all at 1st, it will make it very difficult to put the model together. I highly recommend you have either a razor blade or thin sharp knife available to help remove the pieces. If you simply use your fingers, you could easily break a piece.

I must admit that I am not a person who likes to build models. So it took me about an hour and ½ to put this together. It turned out okay, but not as perfect as the pictures. The shingles do not fit perfectly. Nonetheless I think it looks okay.

Also, when you get to pieces 12, 13, 14 and 15 which is part of instruction number 5… Those 4 pieces make a little platform. The way the instruction show it on instruction number 9, that platform sits inside section B. But if you place it there, then the top shingle portion sits on top of the platform and is not sturdy. If you don’t put that platform there, then the top piece see fits in to the bottom piece a which makes it sturdy. Then I use that platform as a base on the bottom to place the temple on top of. Written on that platform is “Temple of Serenity”. So because of that, I think it should go on the bottom is a base anyway. But of course you can do it anyway you want to.

An optional string of LED lights is included. Two AA batteries are required and not included.

text_fidelity_a:
Playin' Possum This is a great family friendly game that people of all ages can play. The concept is simple in that you need to just try to anticipate what others will play, sort of like rock-paper-scissors. But this game can have multiple players at a time and last until someone either collects enough winning cards (pieces of garbage) or is the last player standing.
The caveats are that you have the ability to "play it safe", which can avoid getting out if someone accuses you of trying to steal on your turn. This can lead to many rounds where nothing happens as someone needs to steal or accuse of stealing for the game to progress. It is also possible to start feeling repetitive after some time as the gameplay does not allow for much variation to keep it interesting. For what it is, it is a fun quick game that doesn't require a lot of setup or learning. But don't expect it to last a long time before people want to do something else instead.
text_fidelity_b: Playin' Possum

Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab These days with many kids doing home schooling due to lockdowns, this would be a great home schoolilng science project or lesson.

The age recommendation is for children six and up, however since most of these experiments require the use of a pot of boiling water, I think the manufacturer should increase the age requirement. Parental supervision is of course a great idea. The booklet is easy to understand, however it might be more difficult for younger children to read and understand the instructions.

I only tried the first experiment in the kit and it worked as expected, and it was the easiest, fastest experiment to get results. The instructions were easy to follow. (I also lacked any distilled water which many of the experiment recipes call for). It was fun for me as an adult to try.

I am not sure if this is an option or not, but it would be nice if refills on the "magic water, colors, (maybe even some not available in this kit) and paper cones) were made available so kids (or adults) can continue to keep playing and making different crystals. (Alum powder and food coloring are both readily available at any grocer.)

The box is attractively marked and would make a great gift for any adult or child who likes science or educational toys. This kit is compatible with other chemistry sets available from the same company.

All in all, it's a fun, educational kit that anyone can enjoy. The only true down side is that it may try the patience of kids who like instant results. Some of these experiments take two or three days to have decent crystals develop. I liked the kit and found it fascinating. I can't wait to try the other experiments in the kit.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs Colorful Crystal Lab STEM Experiment Kit & Lab Setup | Awesome Geometric Crystals, Dazzling Displays, with 11 Shiny, Sparkly, Safe Experiments | Stickers to Decorate Your Lab
